items.stem:
Kulkarni Enterprises, Dehradun, has applied to a bank for a loan of ₹10 lakh. The bank asks for its trading and profit and loss account and its balance sheet for the last three years. A supplier and the owner Imran also study the same statements.
(i) What will the bank look for in each statement? (ii) State one need each of the supplier and the owner.
items.answer: (i) Profit and loss account: profitability and ability to pay interest; balance sheet: liquidity, existing debts and assets available as security. (ii) Supplier: ability to pay dues on time (current assets vs current liabilities). Owner: profit earned and return on capital.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Profit and loss account: profitability and ability to pay interest; balance sheet: liquidity, existing debts and assets available as security. (ii) Supplier: ability to pay dues on time (current assets vs current liabilities). Owner: profit earned and return on capital.

items.stem:
Ananya runs Joshi Stores and says, "My business is small; I know my profit from my cash box, so I do not need financial statements."
(i) Explain why the cash box cannot show the profit. (ii) Give two other reasons why she needs financial statements.
items.answer: (i) Cash ignores credit sales and purchases, outstanding and prepaid items, stock and depreciation; profit is not the same as cash. (ii) To get bank loans and supplier credit; for income tax and GST assessment; to compare performance over years.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Cash ignores credit sales and purchases, outstanding and prepaid items, stock and depreciation; profit is not the same as cash. (ii) To get bank loans and supplier credit; for income tax and GST assessment; to compare performance over years.
